incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), a statutory body under the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition, operating through the CIPC e-Services portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: CoR 14.1 Notice of Incorporation together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) and CoR 9 Consent to Act as Directors
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a Proprietary Limited company under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; share consideration is determined by the board subject to the s4 solvency and liquidity test, and no escrow account capital deposit is mandatory for standard incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers' share subscription set out in the Memorandum of Incorporation is ratified and accepted, and the directors confirm that the solvency and liquidity test under section 4 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 is satisfied. RESOLVED further that the registered office and postal address recorded on the Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) are adopted, and the formation instruments filed with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission are ratified. RESOLVED further that [Name] as Director, [Name] as Chief Executive Officer, and [Name] as Company Secretary or Accounting Officer are confirmed. The directors are authorized to open bank accounts, execute contracts, appoint a registered auditor, and take all ancillary actions. Effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search against the CIPC register to ensure the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing entity; file the BNE-1 name reservation application online, providing a brief descriptive memorandum where the name contains functional elements such as 'Random Video Match App'.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the applicant's identity document or passport
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or opposed, file a letter of motivation on CIPC letterhead; alternatively select and reserve a new name; third-party objections are opposable under section 160 of the Companies Act within the prescribed notice period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of MOI and Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African attorney or registered company practitioner acting for CIPC filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation in conformity with the Companies Regulations 2011, including share capital structure, pre-emptive rights, director powers, and quorum provisions; complete and sign Form CoR 14.1; each subscriber and director must execute the documents and the signatures are certified by a commissioner of oaths before submission.
required_dossiers: Subscriber declaration and authority to incorporate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Minor drafting defects may be cured by filing a corrective amendment under CoR 14.1A prior to the original application being processed; if the documents are queried, CIPC returns a compliance notice identifying the exact defect for immediate correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission to CIPC and Payment of Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the CIPC e-Services account, select 'Company Registration', upload the executed MOI, CoR 14.1 and CoR 9 forms, and pay the prescribed registration fee via the CIPC payment gateway; retain the payment receipt and system-generated submission reference number.
required_dossiers: Payment receipt or payment authorisation reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected for non-compliance or incomplete data, rectify the prescribed defects and re-submit within 20 business days before the application lapses; appeal or objection routes under section 191 of the Companies Act remain available for wrongful refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Registered Office Recordal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, CIPC issues a Computer-generated Certificate of Incorporation bearing the unique company registration number; verify that the registered office address and postal address appear correctly on the public register and retain the certificate as evidence of corporate existence for SARS and banking purposes.
required_dossiers: Certified extract of company registration record
Confirmatory notice of registered office and postal address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or register contains typographical or factual errors, apply to CIPC for rectification under section 82 of the Companies Act using the prescribed CoR correction form without additional substantive filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Tax Registration and COIDA Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) and Department of Employment and Labour (Compensation Fund)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company at SARS for income tax (ITREG), employer PAYE and UIF (EMP-reg), and, if taxable supplies exceed or are expected to exceed ZAR 1 million, VAT (VATREG); simultaneously register for COIDA at the Compensation Fund and, where applicable, at the Unemployment Insurance Fund employment office; provide the SARS registration forms together with corporate and bank documentation.
required_dossiers: SARS Business Registration Form (EMP / IT / VAT)
Company bank account confirmation of particulars
Directors' and employees' certified identity documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: SARS may issue a verification query or administrative penalty for late registration; respond through eFiling or a SARS branch appointment with reasonable cause mitigation, and apply for penalty waiver under section 212 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 if the delay is justified.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: City of Johannesburg Metropolitan Municipality (Business Registration and Zoning Office) together with the Department of Employment and Labour Occupational Health and Safety Directorate
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificate of Compliance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 and Municipal Business Trading Privilege / Zoning Clearance Certificate

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE), administered through the Gauteng Provincial Environmental Authority under the National Environmental Management Act 107 of 1998
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (Registration-Only regime) - office and data-hosting operations under ISIC 6311 are not listed activities under Government Notice R983/984 Listing Notices 1-3, and therefore no formal Environmental Impact Assessment Report is required; only a general environmental duty of care and municipal waste registration apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial effluent discharge to natural water resources; sewage and trade effluent limited to municipal sewer capacity under the Water Services Act 108 of 1997; standby generator and ventilation emissions below the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004 atmospheric emission licensing threshold; electronic waste and server hardware disposal to registered recyclers in accordance with SANS 10248 and the Hazardous Waste Regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Compliance Certificate under SANS 10400 Part T and NFPA 101 issued by the municipal fire authority; Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 workplace clearance for office, server, and technical work areas; structural integrity certificate from a SACPCMP-registered professional engineer; Electrical Certificate of Compliance under SANS 10142-1; and Compensation Fund Letter of Good Standing confirming COIDA registration for all employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); operational portal: SARS eFiling (www.sarsefiling.co.za), supplemented by SARS branch walk-in services and registered tax practitioners; export customs processing via SARS Customs division through the SARS EDI/Web pockets.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A South African incorporated (Pty) Ltd is automatically registered for income tax by SARS following CIPC incorporation via the CIPC-SARS data integration, and receives an income tax reference number. VAT registration is effected on form VAT 101 (company application) submitted through eFiling or a SARS branch within 21 days after the company's taxable turnover exceeds ZAR 1,000,000 in a rolling 12-month period; voluntary VAT registration is available from an annual turnover of ZAR 50,000. Foreign-incorporated entities or foreign branches must apply for a SARS income tax reference number manually by submitting the DA 185/IT-REG application with certified incorporation documents, Memorandum of Incorporation, proof of registered address in South Africa, and identification of directors; the issued SARS tax reference number is then used for VAT registration. For non-resident suppliers of 'electronic services' to South African residents, a separate VAT registration via the SARS eFiling 'foreign vendor' channel is mandatory when supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in 12 months.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - the (Pty) Ltd is a South African resident company taxed in its own right at a flat corporate income tax rate of 27% for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023 (28% for earlier years); there is no pass-through election available for a company. Dividends declared by the company are subject to a 20% dividends tax withheld at source, and the company remains within the South African territorial tax net with worldwide residence-based taxation of its income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime exists in South Africa. Statutory elections available to the Pty Ltd include: (i) headquarter company election under section 9I of the Income Tax Act (conferring a 0% rate on foreign dividends, interest and royalties where the company meets the 80% foreign-shareholding and services thresholds); (ii) intra-group reorganisation and loss-grouping elections under sections 41-47 of the Income Tax Act; (iii) voluntary VAT group registration election under section 52 of the VAT Act for connected persons; (iv) debt-instrument effective interest rate election under section 24J; (v) R&D tax incentive approval election under section 11D; (vi) automatic application of hybrid mismatch rules under sections 8J-8M, with taxpayer ordering choices for the primary and defensive deduction-denial rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS as a single-stage national consumption tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory ZAR 1,000,000 taxable turnover within a rolling 12-month period, applied on a continuous forward-looking basis; voluntary registration from ZAR 50,000 annual turnover. Non-resident suppliers of electronic services to South African residents must register from the same ZAR 1,000,000 threshold in respect of supplies made to South African customers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping, or government pre-clearance for e-invoices. Suppliers must issue a full tax invoice within 21 days of the time of supply, containing section 20 requirements (seller and buyer names and addresses, SARS VAT numbers, aggregate value, VAT amount, tax invoice serial number, date of issue, description, and quantity). SARS accepts electronic invoices under the Electronic Communications and Transactions Act and has published an e-invoicing policy roadmap; submission to SARS is at data level via eFiling (VAT 201 returns), with automated reconciliation against banking, customs and CIPC data. There is no nationally mandated digital signature stamp, but SARS may require interoperability, audit trails and valid electronic signature authentication during VAT audits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports are zero-rated under section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act where goods are supplied to a non-resident under an agreement of sale, delivered to an address outside South Africa, and the exporter obtains and retains documentary proof of physical export within 90 days of the time of supply. Services are zero-rated under section 11(1)(h) where supplied to a non-resident recipient who is not present in South Africa at the time of supply and where the services are not supplied for use in South Africa; for a video-match social telephony app, cross-border subscription, virtual-currency and advertising services delivered to non-resident end-users qualify as zero-rated exports if the company maintains geo-location logs, IP verification, foreign payment-rail settlement evidence (Apple IAP, Paymentwall) and marketing documentation demonstrating the offshore consumer base. Supplies to South African residents remain standard-rated at 15%; reverse-charge rules and section 54A foreign electronic services provisions apply only to non-resident suppliers making supplies into South Africa.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SARS SAD500/Electronic DA 500) or, for digital services, a certificate of export/foreign supply evidence package
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / electronic cargo movement reference for physical goods; for pure digital services, platform payment settlement reports proving non-resident receipt
Foreign-Currency Inward Transfer (FCIT) certificate issued by a SARB Authorised Dealer (local bank) evidencing receipt of the export sales proceeds
Tax invoice and underlying service agreement showing non-resident billing address, user IP-geolocation logs, and payment-rail settlement statements from Apple IAP and Paymentwall
SARB exchange-control declaration (Form 561/Exports or manual export proceeds record) where an Authorised Dealer dispensation applies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may claw back zero-rated treatment and assess output VAT at 15% if export documentation is absent or the export/foreign supply is not effected within the statutory 90-day window for goods or 180-day FX repatriation period. Late-received export proceeds are subject to SARS/SARB audit on foreign exchange compliance; SARS may raise additional assessments within 5 years of assessment, or 10 years in fraud cases. Under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011, an understatement penalty of between 10% and 200% of the shortfall applies, with aggravating factors producing the higher tiers; interest accrues at the SARS prescribed late-payment rate (approximately 10%-11.5% p.a. in 2024/2025, quoted quarterly). Deliberate fraudulent zero-rating is a criminal offence punishable by a fine and/or imprisonment of up to five years, and personal liability may attach to directors or trust beneficiaries under common-law fraud, lifting of the corporate veil, or section 6 VAT provisions where the entity is used as a conduit for VAT evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) - Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933, the Exchange Control Regulations (1961), the SARB Currency and Exchanges Manual for Authorised Dealers, and the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA); day-to-day exchange control administration is delegated to Authorised Dealers (registered commercial banks) and Authorised Dealers with Limited Authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African Rand (ZAR) is a controlled but practically convertible currency on current account. Current-account transactions - including export of digital platform services, app store revenue, advertising services, data processing and software licensing - are liberalised and may be executed freely through an Authorised Dealer, subject to documentary verification (contracts, invoices, PSP payout reports) and mandatory balance-of-payments (BOP) reporting. Capital-account transactions remain regulated: inbound direct investment (share subscription) does not require prior FinSurv approval but must be reported to the Authorised Dealer on the prescribed inward direct investment/BOP declaration, supported by board resolutions, the share register and the Companies Act 71 of 2008 issuance mechanics. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is permitted by the Authorised Dealer without prior SARB approval provided: (i) the company holds a valid SARS tax compliance status; (ii) dividends are declared legally from distributable profits per a board resolution; (iii) the non-resident shareholding is properly recorded; (iv) dividend withholding tax (20%, treaty-reduced where applicable) is deducted and remitted to SARS; and (v) the remittance is reported on the BOP return. Remaining hurdles for this entity: any SARS filing lapse will freeze remittances; UBO transparency under FICA 2023 must be complete; service-export proceeds must be repatriated within the statutory window; and any offshore bank account or offshore treasury vehicle requires prior FinSurv approval, which is generally refused for a fully resident operating (Pty) Ltd.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For services exports (including app store collections via Apple IAP and Paymentwall), foreign currency proceeds must be received in South Africa within 30 days of the date the service is rendered; for goods exports the window is 180 days. The pre-2017 rule mandating conversion of 50% of export proceeds has been abolished, so the required mandatory conversion ratio is 0%, provided the proceeds are either: (a) sold immediately into the interbank market through an Authorised Dealer, or (b) retained in an SARB-approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA) held with an Authorised Dealer. Amounts not retained in an FCA must be converted to ZAR on receipt and reported on the BOP service-export return. For the Company, every Apple and Paymentwall payout statement must evidence the underlying user transactions and the funds must land in the South African operational account within the 30-day window to avoid a contravention of the Authorised Dealer Manual and attendant bank compliance action.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary treasury rail; Medium only as a supplementary settlement corridor. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise Business, Airwallex, Payoneer, Currencycloud, Mercury) cannot provide a domestic ZAR account or clear ZAR payments without being licensed as a bank or registered as an Authorised Dealer under the Banks Act 94 of 1990 and the National Payment System Act 78 of 1998. A South African resident company is also prohibited from maintaining an offshore bank account without prior SARB FinSurv approval, which is rarely granted to a fully resident operating entity; consequently, treasury funds must sit onshore with an Authorised Dealer. EMIs remain commercially viable only as the payout/settlement gateway used by Apple and Paymentwall from their licensed acquiring entities, or as a disbursement rail for small vendor payments where the foreign vendor is paid directly by the EMI from funds remitted outbound under the relevant current-account dispensation. The Company must not maintain float, user funds, or capital injection proceeds in any unlicensed EMI, as such routing would trigger a bank rejection and exchange-control contravention.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid mandate with a de facto physical interview requirement. FICA permits risk-based remote onboarding using biometric/video e-KYC, but South African commercial banks, when faced with a Medium-Risk-Enhanced cross-border video chat app with foreign shareholders, will in practice require: (i) at least one natural-person director or the appointed AML Compliance Officer to attend an in-person interview at the bank's corporate banking suite in Johannesburg (Sandton) or Cape Town; (ii) all other directors and ultimate beneficial owners to complete remote video verification through the bank's FICA-compliant e-KYC channel with notarised passports; (iii) the physical interview to be completed before any outbound payment functionality is activated (inbound-only escrow may be opened earlier at the bank's discretion); and (iv) if all directors are non-resident, the bank will typically decline the application unless a South African physical registered office, a resident director or authorised representative, and a SARS tax referral number/pin are established first.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Random video chat/social app characterised as adult entertainment, dating, or illicit-content facilitator (reputational and terrorist-financing risk)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform content-control pack: mandatory 18+ age gating; AI-powered real-time image/video moderation with human review; verified sign-up identity (phone verification, Apple ID, social linkage); published community standards with automatic ban/block functionality; certification that no adult sexual content is permitted; POPIA-compliant privacy notice; evidence of IP geoblocking of sanctioned and high-risk jurisdictions; and a board-approved user anti-money-laundering/counter-financing-of-terrorism policy aligned with FIC obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregated and intermingled settlement flows from Apple IAP and Paymentwall, where the bank cannot distinguish the Company's net revenue from third-party client money or PSP float
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant-of-record and funds-flow map: Apple Developer Program License Agreement proving Apple collects from the end user and remits the developer share net of commission (Apple acts as merchant of record); Paymentwall merchant agreement proving the Company is merchant of record and Paymentwall acts only as a payment processor with client funds held in segregated safeguarded accounts at regulated institutions; monthly payout statements from Apple and Paymentwall; a one-to-many transaction audit trail (user ID, purchase ID, amount, app-store validation receipt); and a signed director's attestation that no third-party client money is held, controlled, or commingled by the Company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders or opaque ultimate beneficial ownership, including rapid share transfers or funding originating from a weak-AML jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC Beneficial Ownership register (BCS-BEN filing) and FIC UBO confirmation; notarised passports/IDs of all shareholders and natural-person UBOs; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds affidavits with supporting bank statements; banker's reference letters from the remitting foreign banks; a full corporate structure chart to ultimate individuals; and a South African legal opinion confirming compliance with the Companies Act and exchange-control inward listing requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SARS and corporate regulatory non-compliance flags (unfiled tax returns, lapsed CIPC status, unpaid withholding taxes, no POPIA registration)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid SARS Tax Compliance Status (TCS) pin and interim tax reference; CIPC annual return and company registration extract; signed/audited opening financial statements evidencing share capital; VAT registration (if turnover exceeds R1m) with confirmation that app-store exports are zero-rated; dividend withholding tax computation; POPIA Information Officer registration and PAIA manual; and the entity's FICA Risk Management and Compliance programme.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure because global user payments are routed via US/EU/UK PSPs (Apple, Paymentwall) and user traffic may originate in OFAC/UN-sanctioned states or FATF grey-listed countries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Geoblocking configuration excluding sanctioned IP ranges; app-store country availability matrix excluding sanctioned territories; sanctions-screening policy applied to PSP settlement files against OFAC, EU, UN and South African FIC lists; contractual right to suspend payouts from sanctioned users; written compliance attestations from Apple and Paymentwall confirming their own sanctions screening; and a board-approved Sanctions and Asset Freezing policy.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for non-resident equity injection: (1) the non-resident shareholder remits USD/EUR by SWIFT MT103 to the Company's FCA or the Authorised Dealer's inward nostro account in South Africa; (2) the Company files with the bank: board resolution authorising the share issue, updated Memorandum of Incorporation, share subscription agreement, source-of-funds evidence, and the prescribed inward direct investment/BOP return (successor to the legacy Form FIE) within 30 days of receipt; (3) the bank applies the SARB BOP purpose code for direct investment equity, converts to ZAR at the interbank rate, and credits the operational account only after the share issue is recorded in the share register; (4) for shareholder loans, a written loan agreement is executed, the inward loan is reported to the Authorised Dealer, interest must be at arm's length, and repayment requires loan reporting, 15% interest withholding tax (treaty-reduced where applicable) and SARS TCS verification; (5) no injection may be routed through unlicensed EMIs, personal accounts, crypto exchanges, or offshore trusts without prior FinSurv approval; (6) the bank will perform sanctions screening of the remitting bank and confirm the FIC 2023 UBO registration before releasing funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail: SWIFT MT103 international credit transfer (TT) for all operating payments - cloud and bandwidth (AWS, Google Cloud, Cloudflare), digital marketing (Meta, Google, TikTok), software subscriptions, contractor and KYC vendor fees, and platform fees to Apple/Paymentwall where not netted. Outbound current-account payments require no prior SARB approval, but the Authorised Dealer demands a valid VAT/tax invoice, service contract, proof of service performance, and the correct SARB BOP purpose code (e.g., computer and information services, telecommunications, advertising/media). Related-party payments require transfer-pricing documentation under s31 of the Income Tax Act; royalties require DWT at 15% (treaty-reduced) and SARS documentary confirmation. For significant import-heavy capital expenditure (servers, head-end hardware), a Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP600) through the bank's trade desk is available and recommended above large open-account TTs. Funds can be paid from the Company's USD FCA to minimise FX spread. Payments must be made within 30 days (services) or 180 days (goods) of service/goods delivery; cash advances, cryptocurrency transfers, and personal-account aggregations are prohibited.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot USD/ZAR and EUR/ZAR conversion through an Authorised Dealer - mandatory on receipt for proceeds not retained in an approved FCA; no separate approval required.

Outright Deliverable Forward Exchange Contract (FEC) on USD/ZAR or EUR/ZAR - the primary permitted hedge; maximum tenor 12 months; must be supported by demonstrable underlying exposure (expected Apple IAP and Paymentwall settlement inflows and committed USD vendor payables); executed under a bank master agreement (ISDA/SAFEX equivalent) with margin/collateral and quarterly re-validation.

FX Swaps (FEC rollover / spot-forward swaps) - permitted for cash-flow timing mismatches between USD receipts and ZAR disbursements, provided the swap is executed with the same Authorised Dealer and the tenor remains within the underlying trade cycle.

Cross-Currency Swaps - permissible only with prior Authorised Dealer/FinSurv approval, typically limited to material long-dated USD liabilities (e.g., capitalised shareholder loans); not economically necessary for this app treasury below ZAR 250m notional and therefore excluded from the initial hedging blueprint.
Vanilla FX Options - not a standard corporate product for ZAR; available only on a bespoke basis with FinSurv consent for proven hedging requirements; excluded from the initial plan.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) - structurally inapplicable for a resident company because the ZAR has a fully deliverable onshore interbank market; executing an NDF offshore would constitute unauthorised exchange-control avoidance; non-resident counterparties may use NDFs only outside South Africa.

Natural and commercial hedges - mandatory as the baseline: USD-denominated vendor contracting matched to USD inflows, maintenance of a working-capital USD FCA balance, and an automatic 5-business-day conversion policy to cap unhedged ZAR exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of R50 (approx. USD 2.70) per month up to a maximum of R150 (approx. USD 8); persistent non-compliance leads to deregistration/strike-off after 2 years of consecutive failure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the Annual Return filing; due within 30 business days of anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Included in the Annual Return filing; failure to submit BO information may result in CIPC enforcement action, administrative fines up to ZAR 500 (approx. USD 27) per month, and potential director liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Income Tax Return (ITR14) for corporate tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Twelve months after the company's financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties of 5% of unpaid tax per month (up to 30%) plus interest at SARS prescribed rate; persistent non-compliance can trigger criminal prosecution and asset attachment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder meeting (AGM) and resolution filing (if required)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First AGM within 18 months of incorporation, thereafter at least once every calendar year but no more than 15 months apart
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene AGM is a legal irregularity; special resolutions not filed within 30 business days attract late filing penalties of up to ZAR 300 (approx. USD 16).

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit required if public interest score (PIS) >= 350; or if PIS is 100-349, an independent review (not audit) is required. PIS is computed on basis of employees, third-party liability, and turnover. A private company (Pty) Ltd with only shareholders' interests may still exceed 350 depending on scale; the company must calculate PIS annually and maintain a record.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for SMEs (under South African Companies Act), or full IFRS if required by public interest score, or if the company is listed or state-owned; local GAAP allowed for non-entities with below threshold.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must annually confirm beneficial ownership details with CIPC at the time of filing the Annual Return, and also update within 10 business days of any shareholding change. Required details include natural persons with direct or indirect ownership >5%, control via voting rights, and senior managing officials. A record of beneficial ownership must be maintained at the registered office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of shareholder meetings and board meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200 - 500 for registered office and/or company secretary services in major metropolitan areas
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - 4,000 for a medium-risk private company depending on complexity, transaction volume, and cross-border transactions

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holidays. Preferential deductions available under section 11D for research and development (up to 150% deduction for qualifying R&D expenditure), and the Venture Capital Company (VCC) regime under section 12J allowing investors a deduction of up to 100% of qualifying investments. Special economic zone (SEZ) tax allowance under section 12R provides reduced corporate income tax rate of 15% for qualifying SEZ operations, subject to approval. These are not applicable to a typical video-match app without qualifying R&D or SEZ location.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed via SARS eFiling (electronic filing system).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 12 months from the end of the company's financial year end, unless a shorter period is prescribed by SARS in a notice; provisional tax returns (IRP6) due semi-annually.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income (worldwide income for residents; South African sourced income for non-residents).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident company must include only income from a South African source; foreign-source income excluded unless effectively connected to a South African permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income (e.g. certain dividends received, foreign dividends under participation exemption).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident should claim exemptions only if supported by DTA provisions and domestic exemption sections.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after allowable deductions and set-off of assessed losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident may deduct expenses actually incurred in production of South African income; no set-off of foreign losses against SA income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable at 27% on taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a DTA applies and a permanent establishment exists, tax is limited to the PE's attributable profits; otherwise full 27% on SA-source business income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisional tax payments made (IRP6) for the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident with a PE in South Africa is a provisional taxpayer; payments due six months after start and on year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessed loss carried forward from prior years (limited to 5 years for certain losses incurred post-2020).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident may carry forward SA assessed losses derived from SA-source activities; not foreign losses.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of up to 10% of the amount of tax assessed (minimum SAR 500 per month of non-compliance, capped at 20% of tax). Under the Tax Administration Act, a fixed percentage-based penalty of 10% of assessed tax per month for failure to submit a return, with a maximum of 20 months; additional daily surcharge of 0.5% per month on unpaid tax, plus interest at the prescribed rate. SARS may impose administrative penalties of up to SAR 5,000 per month for non-submission of a return, and criminal penalties for intentional non-compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a South African Revenue Service (SARS) tax residence certificate (TRC) from the treaty jurisdiction, complete a declaration via the SARS eFiling portal, and attach the TRC and a DTA relief application form (as applicable). SARS confirms treaty entitlement and reduces the dividend withholding tax rate to the applicable treaty rate (often 5%–15% depending on ownership percentage and treaty). For royalties and interest, the payor must withhold at the lower treaty rate only after receiving the recipient's TRC and completing a SARS-approved relief declaration.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: interest withholding tax 15%; royalty withholding tax 15%. Treaty rates may be reduced to 0% for interest under most DTAs and to 0%–10% for royalties depending on the treaty and IP character (e.g. South Africa–US DTA: royalties generally 0%, interest 0% if beneficial owner is US resident; many African and European DTAs provide 5%–10% royalty rates).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: ZAR 100 million (total gross receipts) or ZAR 50 million in certain cross-border related-party transactions; Local File / Master File thresholds per SARS Notice may require documentation if annual cross-border related-party transactions exceed ZAR 5 million, and a Country-by-Country Report is mandatory for groups with consolidated group revenue above ZAR 10 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa applies the Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) through SARS transfer-pricing and controlled foreign company (CFC) rules, and through the general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR). A company must demonstrate real economic substance (board meetings, key decisions, staff, assets and risk in South Africa) to justify the tax residence and profit allocation; absence of substance triggers recharacterisation, denial of treaty benefits, and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of South African-source digital revenue from video-chat fees and virtual gifts, fabrication of expense deductions, or concealment of beneficial ownership of the South African entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Tax Administration Act No. 28 of 2011: understatement penalty of 25%–200% of the understated tax depending on conduct (substantial understatement, reasonable care not taken, gross negligence, intentional tax evasion); criminal conviction liable to fine of up to SAR 50,000 or imprisonment up to 5 years, or both.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for the company's unpaid tax if they knowingly caused or allowed the company to fail to pay tax; SARS may issue a notice of personal liability under section 155 of the Tax Administration Act. Directors face civil restitution for amounts wrongfully diverted, travel bans (withdrawal of passport / blocking departure from South Africa), and criminal imprisonment up to 5 years for fraudulent evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: South African entity with no office, no employees, no real decision-making, and no operational substance while booking large profits from a video-match app, particularly with related-party digital routing through low-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS may disregard the entity as a sham, reallocate income to the owner or connected persons under transfer-pricing rules, and levy an additional assessment plus 150%–200% understatement penalties. The entity may be struck off by the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) for failure to comply with beneficial ownership filing and annual return filing requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for company debts (including tax liabilities) if the company carries on business recklessly or with gross negligence (section 22 of the Companies Act). Directors face director disqualification, personal restitution orders, and possible criminal sanction for reckless trading.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the video-chat app platform through Paymentwall / Apple IAP rails to launder proceeds of crime, accept anonymous payments, obscure the origin of user funds, or move profits without beneficial ownership disclosure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA) No. 38 of 2001: administrative fines of up to SAR 10 million for contraventions (failing to conduct customer due diligence, failing to report suspicious and unusual transactions); criminal penalties of up to 10 years imprisonment for money laundering activities under the Prevention of Organised Crime Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly or negligently fail to implement AML controls are personally liable for penalties, may have their assets frozen, be subjected to travel bans, and face imprisonment up to 10 years. SARS and the FIC may also impose personal confiscation orders for funds laundered through the corporate vehicle.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cross-border payment of excessive royalties or fees to a related offshore IP owner with no demonstrable services, or under-pricing of rights granted to a foreign affiliate, thereby shifting profits away from South Africa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS adjusts the taxable income to an arm's-length price, disallows the deduction in full, and applies an understatement penalty of 50%–200% on the additional tax. Specific interest and late-payment penalties are applied to the adjusted amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable if they participated in or knowingly allowed transfer-pricing documentation to be false or misleading, or if the company remains non-compliant after a SARS demand. Imprisonment for tax fraud (up to 5 years) and travel bans apply.
